terms.gloss: what's the matter? what's going on?
terms.grammar: negōtī, partitive genitive of negōtium (the older form of negōtiī)
evidence: Plaut. Most. 2.2.27; Plaut. Capt. 3.5.11: quid negōtī est, quamobrem suscēnsēs mihi? (Lewis & Short), s.v. negōtium

terms.gloss: what's going on? how are things?
evidence: Ter. Ad. 373–374: Hem, Dēmea, haud aspexeram tē. Quid agitur?
terms.comment: In comedy also the greeting “how are things?” (see how are you).
Traupman’s phrase; not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

phrases.latin: Hem, Dēmea, haud aspexeram tē. Quid agitur?
phrases.english: Oh, Demea, I didn’t see you. How are things?

sources: Lewis & Short: negotium · Lewis & Short: ago
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 99, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Ter. Ad. 373–374 from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-terentius), checked against the edition named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
